# From Paperwork to Progress: How Nebraska DMV Is Modernizing Compliance


October 13, 2026


by Juliette Thompson


##


Government agencies face increasing pressure to process growing volumes of documents while maintaining accuracy, compliance, and efficient service delivery. For the Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV), managing hundreds of thousands of vehicle identification number (VIN) records requires significant staff resources and careful oversight.


To help streamline these processes, the Nebraska DMV is leveraging Tyler Technologies' Document Automation platform, building on the agency's broader modernization strategy and commitment to improving operational efficiency.


## Bringing Greater Efficiency to VIN Validation


As part of its implementation, the Nebraska DMV will use Tyler's Document Automation platform to support motor carrier VIN validation processes. The solution is expected to provide 100% audit capability across nearly 500,000 VIN records, helping the agency strengthen compliance while reducing the burden of manual review.


By automating document-driven workflows, the DMV can improve accuracy of record validation while providing staff with more time to focus on supporting residents and addressing complex service needs.


## Transforming High-Volume Document Processes


For many government agencies, compliance-related workflows require employees to manually review, validate, and process large volumes of documentation. These tasks are often time-consuming, repetitive, and vulnerable to human error.


Document Automation helps agencies modernize these operations by automatically extracting, validating, and processing information from documents, enabling teams to work more efficiently while maintaining oversight and accountability.


For Nebraska, applying intelligent automation to VIN validation not only creates an opportunity to improve audit readiness and operational transparency, but will also help the DMV recognize a nearly 150% cost avoidance year over year by implementing Document Automation.


## Part of a Broader Digital Transformation Strategy


The expansion of Document Automation is part of Nebraska's broader effort to modernize the delivery of government services. Alongside the automation initiative, the state is also deploying Tyler's Resident AI Assistant statewide following a successful DMV pilot, which lead to over 100,000 questions in 3 months, serves 50 languages, and reduced call volumes by 20% while driving more transactions online.


Together, these investments reflect a growing focus on using technology to improve operational efficiency, expand access to services, and support data-driven decision-making across government.


Tyler’s Document Automation platform is designed specifically for the unique requirements of government agencies. The combination of public sector expertise, secure technology, and configurable workflows allows agencies to modernize critical operations while maintaining compliance and accountability.


As governments continue to evaluate opportunities for digital transformation, Nebraska's approach demonstrates how document automation can deliver measurable operational benefits while helping agencies better serve the people who rely on them every day.
